en: to review; to examine carefully (a plan, document, proposal)

examples.ko: 보내기 전에 한 번 더 검토해요.
examples.en: I review it once more before sending.
I reviewed the plan carefully.
The team leader is reviewing the documents.
I'll look into whether there's a good way.
I'll contact you right after I've reviewed the contents.
There are so many documents to review that it's tiring.

explain: '확인하다'는 맞는지 보는 것이고, '검토하다'는 좋은지 나쁜지 따져 보고 결정하려고 살피는 거예요. 직장에서 '검토해 볼게요'는 바로 정하지 않겠다는 뜻일 때가 많아요. '검토 중이에요'처럼 '중'을 붙여 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: We are reviewing that plan right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: '중'을 붙여 지금 살펴보고 있고 아직 정하지 않았다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 중 means you are looking at it now and have not decided yet.

phrases.en: That's a good idea. I'll look into it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바로 정하지 않고 살펴보겠다는 부드러운 대답이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A soft reply meaning you will look at it before deciding.

phrases.en: I was busy, so I haven't been able to review the documents yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '못'과 같은 뜻으로, 하고 싶었지만 하지 못했다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says you wanted to review but could not.

explain_en: '확인하다' is checking whether something is right, while 검토하다 is weighing the pros and cons in order to decide. At work, '검토해 볼게요' often means 'I won't decide right now'. People often add 중 and say '검토 중이에요' (it's under review).

examples.en: My younger brother isn't really focused on fishing and just talks.
I go fishing by the river every weekend.

examples.ko: 낚시질에 빠진 뒤로 집에 잘 안 있어요.
examples.en: Ever since he got hooked on fishing, he's hardly ever at home.
Fishing is prohibited at this lake.
I bought bait before going fishing.

examples.ko: 처음 한 낚시질이라 아무것도 못 잡았어요.
examples.en: It was my first time fishing, so I caught nothing.

explain: 일상에서는 '낚시'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. '낚시질'은 낚시하는 일 자체를 말할 때 쓰고, '-질'이 붙어 조금 투박하게 들릴 수 있어요. 보통은 '낚시를 하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I go fishing on weekends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '낚시질'보다 '낚시'를 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily speech 낚시 is used more than 낚시질.

phrases.en: The man is fishing at the lake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사로 쓰면 낚시하는 모습을 그대로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: As a verb, it describes the act of fishing directly.

phrases.en: Every weekend I go to the river to fish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목적을 말할 때 '-러 가다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with -러 가다 to state a purpose.

explain_en: In daily life '낚시' sounds much more natural. '낚시질' refers to the act of fishing itself, and with '-질' it can sound a bit blunt. Usually people say '낚시를 하다'.

examples.en: In winter I went sledding with the kids.
The sledding hill is really crowded on weekends.

examples.ko: 언덕에서 눈썰매가 너무 빨리 내려가서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The sled went down the hill so fast that I was startled.

examples.ko: 눈썰매 타는 게 생각보다 무섭지 않아요.
examples.en: Riding a sled isn't as scary as I thought.

examples.ko: 동생이 눈썰매를 또 타고 싶다고 졸라요.
examples.en: My little brother keeps begging to ride the sled again.

examples.ko: 이번 겨울에는 눈썰매 말고 스키를 배워 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: This winter I want to try learning to ski instead of sledding.

explain: 보통 '눈썰매를 타다'로 말하고, 놀러 가는 곳은 '눈썰매장'이라고 해요. 스키나 스노보드와 달리 앉아서 타기 때문에 아이들도 많이 즐겨요.

phrases.en: The kids ride sleds on the hill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 썰매는 '타다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Sleds go with the verb 타다.

phrases.en: I want to go to a sledding hill this winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈썰매를 타러 가는 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The place you go to ride sleds.

phrases.example: 눈이 많이 와서 눈썰매 타러 갔어요.
phrases.en: It snowed a lot, so we went sledding.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-러 가다'로 목적을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses -러 가다 to state the purpose of going.

explain_en: People usually say '눈썰매를 타다', and the place to go is called '눈썰매장'. Unlike skiing or snowboarding you ride sitting down, so it is popular with kids too.

en: to do a thorough cleaning; to spring-clean

examples.en: Every weekend the whole family gives the house a thorough clean.

examples.ko: 설날 전에 우리는 집 안을 대청소했어요.
examples.en: Before the New Year holiday we cleaned the whole house thoroughly.
We will give the classroom a thorough clean tomorrow afternoon.

examples.ko: 대청소하고 나니까 방이 두 배로 넓어 보여요.
examples.en: After the big clean, the room looks twice as big.

examples.ko: 다 같이 대청소하면 금방 끝날 거예요.
examples.en: If we all do the big clean together, it will be done quickly.
On the day of the big clean, we open all the windows.

explain: '청소하다'는 평소에 하는 청소이고, '대청소하다'는 구석구석까지 크게 하는 청소예요. 명절이나 이사처럼 큰 일을 앞두고 할 때가 있어요. '대청소를 하다'처럼 '대청소'를 명사로 써도 돼요.

phrases.en: I do a big cleaning before moving.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대청소하다'와 같은 뜻이고 명사로 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 대청소하다, using it as a noun.

phrases.example: 손님이 오기 전에 집을 대청소해야 해요.
phrases.en: I have to clean the house thoroughly before guests come.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꼭 해야 하는 일일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it is something you must do.

phrases.en: I'm going to clean my room thoroughly this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 할 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about a future plan.

explain_en: 청소하다 is everyday cleaning, while 대청소하다 is cleaning every corner on a big scale. People may do it before a holiday or a move. You can also use 대청소 as a noun, as in 대청소를 하다.

examples.en: People gathered at the venue from the morning.
We took a bus to the venue.
The venue was so big that I got lost.
After the match we took photos at the venue.
The players cleaned the venue and went home.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 대회장으로 가는 길이 막혔어요.
examples.en: It rained, so the road to the venue was jammed.

explain: '경기장'은 운동 경기를 하는 곳이고, '대회장'은 대회가 열리는 장소 전체를 가리켜요. 그래서 노래 대회나 요리 대회가 열리는 곳도 '대회장'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 우리는 아침 아홉 시에 대회장에 도착했어요.
phrases.en: We arrived at the venue at nine in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대회가 열리는 곳에 왔다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when arriving at the place where the event is held.

phrases.en: The inside of the venue was full of people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대회장의 안쪽을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the inside of the venue.

phrases.en: Let's meet in front of the venue tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 만나는 장소를 정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to set a meeting place.
phrases.en_equiv: to meet in front of the venue

explain_en: 경기장 is the place where a sports match is played, while 대회장 is the whole place where a contest or event is held. So the site of a singing or cooking contest is also called 대회장.

examples.en: I serve coffee at a cafe.
I worked serving at a restaurant every weekend.
There are many customers, so it is hard to serve alone.
The server smiled kindly.

examples.ko: 제가 음식을 서빙할 테니 앉아 계세요.
examples.en: I will serve the food, so please stay seated.
After serving, I washed the dishes right away.

explain: 식당 아르바이트 이야기에서 '서빙을 하다', '서빙 알바'처럼 써요. 음식을 만드는 곳은 '주방', 손님 쪽에서 음식을 나르는 곳은 '홀'이라고 나눠 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: I do serving at a restaurant.
phrases.nuance_ko: '서빙하다'를 '서빙을 하다'로 나눠 말할 수도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb can be split into 서빙 + 을 하다.

phrases.en: On weekends I work a part-time serving job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 하는 아르바이트를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a part-time job at a restaurant.

phrases.en: I served food to the customers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇을 나르는지 앞에 넣어 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the object before it to say what you serve.

explain_en: It shows up in restaurant part-time talk: '서빙을 하다', '서빙 알바'. People sometimes split the work into '주방' (kitchen, where food is made) and '홀' (the floor, where food is carried to customers).

p.n: 내오다 just means bringing the food out; 서빙하다 sounds like working as a server.

en: to join the military; to enlist

examples.en: My older brother enlists next month.
He enlisted right when he turned twenty.
That singer is scheduled to enlist next year.
On the day he enlisted, the whole family saw him off.

examples.ko: 친구는 대학교를 마치고 입대해서 이 년 뒤에 돌아와요.
examples.en: My friend enlisted after finishing university and returns in two years.
Before enlisting, I traveled with friends.

explain: 입대하다는 군대에 들어갈 때 쓰고, 군대에서 나올 때는 '제대하다'를 써요. 한국에서는 남자들이 보통 군대에 가야 해서 자주 나오는 말이에요.

phrases.en: My friend is going into the military next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '입대하다'와 같은 뜻이고, 말할 때 더 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '입대하다', and more casual in speech.

phrases.en: I wrote letters often after I enlisted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군대에 들어간 다음의 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for what happens after joining the military.

phrases.en: The enlistment date has been set.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군대에 들어가는 날을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The day someone goes into the military.

explain_en: 입대하다 is for entering the military, and leaving it is '제대하다'. In Korea men are generally required to serve, so this word comes up often.

examples.en: At work, newcomers usually start by learning odd jobs.
I did nothing but odd jobs all day and then left work.

examples.ko: 잡일이 많아서 정작 중요한 일을 못 했어요.
examples.en: There were so many odd jobs that I couldn't do the really important work.
I earn pocket money helping with odd jobs at a restaurant.

examples.ko: 청소나 심부름 같은 잡일은 제가 할게요.
examples.en: I'll do the odd jobs like cleaning and errands.
Odd jobs are taking up too much of my time.

explain: 특별한 기술이 필요 없는 자잘한 일을 가리켜요. 약간 낮춰 보는 느낌이 있어서 남이 하는 일에 쓰면 실례일 수 있어요. 비슷한 말로 '허드렛일'이 있어요.

phrases.en: Today I did chores at the shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잡일'과 가장 자주 같이 쓰는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the verb most often used with '잡일'.

phrases.en: It's a small shop, so there are a lot of odd jobs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자잘한 일이 많아서 바쁠 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when you are busy with many small tasks.

phrases.en: They only give me menial chores, so it's tiring.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잡일'과 비슷한 말이에요. 중요하지 않은 막일이라는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '잡일', but it carries a stronger feeling of unimportant, menial work.

explain_en: It refers to small tasks that need no special skill. It carries a slightly belittling tone, so using it for someone else's work can be rude. A similar word is '허드렛일'.

examples.en: We timed the running record with a stopwatch.
The teacher pressed the stopwatch.
Please reset the stopwatch to zero.
I installed a stopwatch app on my phone.

examples.ko: 경기 전에 초시계가 고장 나서 새로 샀어요.
examples.en: The stopwatch broke before the match, so I bought a new one.
Stop right away when the stopwatch beeps.

explain: 휴대폰이나 시계 기능에서는 '스톱워치'라는 말도 많이 써요. 시간을 재기 시작할 때는 '초시계를 누르다', 끝낼 때는 '멈추다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I measure time with the stopwatch on my phone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휴대폰이나 시계의 기능을 말할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for the phone or watch feature.

phrases.en: Please press the stopwatch when we start.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시간을 재기 시작할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when starting to time something.

phrases.en: I stopped the stopwatch when he crossed the finish line.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시간을 재는 일을 끝낼 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when ending the timing.

explain_en: On phones and watch functions people also commonly say '스톱워치'. You say '초시계를 누르다' to start timing and '멈추다' to stop it.

examples.en: The treatment room is at the end of the hall on the right.
I went to the treatment room for physical therapy.
Please be quiet inside the treatment room.

examples.ko: 치료실이 넓어서 침대가 여러 개 있어요.
examples.en: The treatment room is large, so it has several beds.
After the checkup, I got an injection in the treatment room.
The nurse showed me to the treatment room.

explain: 병원에서 의사가 진찰하는 곳은 '진료실', 주사나 물리 치료처럼 치료를 하는 곳은 '치료실'이라고 구분해서 말해요. 병원 안내판에서도 자주 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The physical therapy room is on this floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 가장 자주 듣는 '치료실' 종류예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common type of treatment room you hear about in hospitals.

phrases.en: Please wait in front of the treatment room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내할 때 장소를 말하는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to point out a place when giving directions.
phrases.en_equiv: in front of the treatment room

phrases.en: The nurse guided me to the treatment room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 환자를 그곳으로 데려갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone takes a patient to the room.
phrases.en_equiv: to guide to the treatment room

explain_en: In a hospital, the place where the doctor examines you is the '진료실', and the place for injections or physical therapy is the '치료실'. You will often see both on hospital signs.

examples.en: I test the new program first.
I tested the app yesterday and it went well.
I'll tell you about the problems after testing.

examples.ko: 테스트할 때는 여러 번 해 봐야 해요.
examples.en: When you test, you have to try several times.
Please wait a moment while we test.

examples.ko: 신제품을 직접 테스트한 사람이 후기를 썼어요.
examples.en: A person who tested the new product wrote a review.

explain: 제품, 프로그램, 기능이 되는지 확인해 볼 때 써요. 학교 시험은 '시험'이라고 해요. '시험하다'도 있지만 일상 대화에서는 외래어 '테스트'를 자주 들어요.

phrases.example: 출시하기 전에 새 기능을 테스트해 봐요.
phrases.en: We test the new feature before releasing it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보다'를 붙여 한번 해 본다는 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-아/어 보다' gives the feel of trying it out.

phrases.example: 새로 산 기계를 먼저 시험해 봤어요.
phrases.en: I tried out the newly bought machine first.
phrases.nuance_ko: '테스트하다'와 뜻이 같은 한자어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A Sino-Korean word with the same meaning as '테스트하다'.

phrases.en: I run tests on the app every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '테스트'에 '하다'를 붙여 말하는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Combines the noun '테스트' with '하다'.

explain_en: Use it when checking whether a product, program, or feature works. A school exam is called '시험'. '시험하다' also exists, but in daily talk you will hear the loanword '테스트'.

p.n: Grammatical, but the replacement sounds less natural for software.
